newsitem.title: GERMANY: German economic panel criticises revaluation bid.
newsitem.headline: German economic panel criticises revaluation bid.

text.p: The German government's bids to revalue its gold reserves or accelerate the sale of shares in Deutsche Telekom AG are inappropriate as part of a long-term effort to correct the government's financial problems, the Council of Economic Advisors said in a special statement on Wednesday.

The group of academic economists who advise the government on economic policy said the moves would make it hard for Bonn to maintain its stance for a strict interpretation of the entry criteria for European monetary union.
It urged the government to pass a law that would ensure the security of the budget.

In the special report, which was given to Chancellor Helmut Kohl on May 23 but first released to the press on Wednesday, the panel said the proposals themselves were defensible, but that it had been a mistake to float them on the same day that the spring tax estimate showed a large shortfall in government revenues.

"This gives the public and our European partners the impression that Germany too belongs to the group of countries that are trying (to join EMU) through 'creative bookkeeping', a practice that Germany has openly criticised," the letter said.
"The government will find it hard to insist as convincingly as previously on the strict and narrow application of the convergence criteria."
Ad hoc spending freezes and revenue measures are not adequate to the task of budget consolidation, the report said.
"The government will not get past the need to resort to law to package its consolidation strategy for personnel costs, subsidies and social spending. A budget security law will be needed."
